title: Complaint call handoff from your phone host
seoTitle: Complaint call handoff from your phone host | ROAL
description: See how a complaint call handoff should work, what staff should hear, and how a phone host can pass upset callers to the right person.
question: How should a restaurant handle a complaint call handoff from the phone host?
answer: A complaint call handoff should be short, calm, and specific: the phone host should collect the caller’s name, number, and complaint, then pass a clean summary to staff right away. For restaurants using ROAL, complaint calls are handed to staff with the key details so a person can step in and resolve it without making the caller repeat everything.
summary: Set up a simple complaint handoff so upset callers reach the right staff member with the right details.
intro:
A complaint call handoff should move the caller from the phone host to a real person fast, with the reason for the call already clear. The goal is to calm the caller, gather the facts, and let staff take over without making them repeat the same story.

For a restaurant, that usually means one short handoff line, a few must-have details, and a clear place for the note to land. ROAL does this for complaint calls and other tricky requests, while still handling pickup orders, hours, address questions, and menu questions on its own.

sections.h2: What should the phone host say before handing off a complaint call?
sections.body:
Keep the handoff short and plain. The caller should hear that someone is being brought in, not a long explanation.

A good script line is: "I’m going to get a team member to help with that right now." If the caller is upset about the food, the wait, or a wrong order, the phone host should not try to argue or explain the restaurant policy on the spot.

Use a simple handoff checklist:
- Caller name
- Callback number
- Order name or order time, if they have it
- What went wrong
- Whether they want a refund, remake, or call back

That is enough for staff to start. For a pizza shop or deli, the handoff should sound calm and steady, not robotic. The job is to lower the temperature before the conversation reaches the counter or manager.

sections.h2: What details should staff get from a complaint call handoff?
sections.body:
The best complaint call handoff gives staff just enough information to act. If the caller has to repeat everything from scratch, the handoff failed.

Ask the phone host to capture the basics in this order:
1. Name
2. Phone number
3. Order details
4. Complaint summary
5. Urgency level

For example, a caller might say, "My delivery order came missing fries and the sandwich was cold." That should be passed along as a short note, not a full transcript for staff to hunt through.

Here is a simple staff-facing format:

| Field | Example |
|---|---|
| Caller name | Maria |
| Phone | 201-555-0123 |
| Order type | Pickup |
| Problem | Missing side and cold entrée |
| Ask | Wants a manager callback |

ROAL sends a clean summary to staff so the kitchen or manager can decide what to do next. If the caller wants help with an allergy-sensitive issue or a serious complaint, the phone host should hand off immediately instead of guessing.

sections.h2: Which complaint calls should never stay with the phone host?
sections.body:
Some calls need a person right away. The phone host should hand these off instead of trying to solve them alone.

Common examples:
- Allergy-sensitive complaints or concerns
- Missing food or clearly wrong orders
- Requests for a manager
- Threatening or very upset callers
- Catering complaints or large-order problems

A useful phrase is: "I want to make sure the right person sees this now." That sounds better than repeating the complaint back in a cold way.

For restaurants that take a lot of pickup orders, this matters during rushes. The host can keep answering the regular calls, while the complaint goes to staff with a summary. If your team also wants a clean way to track call history, [How it works](/how-it-works) and [Questions owners ask](/faq) are good places to start. The key is simple: fast handoff, no arguing, no long back-and-forth with the caller.

sections.h2: How do you train staff to respond once the handoff lands?
sections.body:
A good handoff is only half the job. The other half is making sure staff know who owns the complaint once it arrives.

Set a basic response order:
1. Read the note.
2. Check the order or ticket.
3. Decide whether to remake, refund, or call back.
4. Contact the guest with one clear answer.

If you run a busy takeout spot, assign one person on each shift to watch complaint notes. That can be the manager, expo, or the counter lead. The caller does not need a perfect policy explanation. They need a quick human answer.

Example staff line:
"Hi, this is the restaurant. I saw your note about the missing appetizer. I’m checking the order now."

That kind of response keeps the conversation calm. It also helps with repeat business, because the guest feels heard. If the staff member needs the order details fast, a system like ROAL can surface the call summary and transcript in the dashboard, which saves a lot of guessing at the counter.

sections.h2: How does a complaint call handoff fit into daily phone operations?
sections.body:
A complaint handoff works best when it is part of the whole phone setup, not an afterthought. You want the same phone line to handle orders, questions, reservations, and complaints in a consistent way.

A practical daily setup looks like this:
- Pickup and delivery orders go straight through
- Hours, address, parking, and menu questions are answered automatically
- Reservation requests are captured for staff
- Complaints and manager requests are handed off with a summary

If you are already forwarding calls from your existing number, keep the rules simple and test them during a quiet time. On many carriers and phone systems, forwarding codes differ, so confirm with your provider and test with a real call. Our [call forwarding codes by carrier](/tools/call-forwarding-codes) page can help you check the common options.

ROAL is built for that kind of flow. It answers the phone, takes orders from the live menu, and passes the tough calls to staff. That means your team can focus on fixing the issue instead of chasing the call.

sections.h2: What does a smart complaint handoff cost compared with other options?
sections.body:
A complaint handoff is not just about service. It also affects labor and call handling costs.

Here is a simple example you can swap for your own numbers:
- Say your average order is $28
- Say one missed complaint call leads to one lost repeat order
- Say you get 20 complaint-related calls in a busy month

Even one poor handoff can cost more than the time it takes to handle it well. Human answering services usually bill per minute or per call, and many AI phone tools charge a fixed monthly fee per location even when orders are slow. ROAL uses a different model: $0.90 per completed phone order, with no monthly fee, no setup fee, and no per-minute fee.

That does not mean every call should be pushed to automation. Tricky calls belong with staff. But a clean complaint handoff means the phone host can keep the line moving while the restaurant handles the real problem. If you want to compare costs for your own shop, [the phone host cost calculator](/tools/phone-host-cost-calculator) and [Pricing](/pricing) are useful next stops.

takeaways: A complaint call handoff should be short, calm, and specific.
Staff need the caller name, number, order details, and the complaint in plain language.
Allergy issues, manager requests, and serious complaints should go to a person fast.
ROAL can hand off tricky calls with a summary while still handling orders and basic questions.
Test your forwarding setup and confirm it with a real call before relying on it.

faq.q: What is a complaint call handoff in a restaurant?
faq.a: It is the process of moving an upset caller from the phone host to a staff member with the important details already collected. The caller should not have to repeat the complaint from scratch. A good handoff keeps the call calm and gives staff a clear starting point.

faq.q: What information should be included in a complaint handoff?
faq.a: At minimum, collect the caller’s name, phone number, order type, what went wrong, and what they want next. If they mention an allergy, a manager request, or a serious service issue, note that clearly. Short and specific is better than long and messy.

faq.q: Should a phone host handle complaints or pass them to staff?
faq.a: Routine questions can stay with the phone host, but complaints should usually go to staff. The host can collect the facts and route the call, while a person decides on the fix. That keeps the caller from getting stuck in a loop.

faq.q: How do I test whether my complaint handoff works?
faq.a: Call your restaurant when it is quiet and act like a guest with a complaint. Check whether the phone host captures the right details and whether staff gets a clear summary. If your calls are forwarded, confirm the forwarding with your carrier or phone system and test it with a real call.
